acip: DES NA STONG NYID KYI DON GTAN LA 'BABS TSUL KHYAD MED KYANG DE'I DON SGOM PAR BYED PA NA, GA-YAS GA-YON GYI RLUNG DH'U T'IR BTZUD NAS DER THIM PA'I DBANG GIS GTUM MO 'BAR BAS BYANG SEMS BZHUS PA'I BDE BA CHEN POS STONG PA'I DON NGES NAS SGOM PA'I LHAN SKYES KYIS SGRIB PA'I BAG CHAGS SBYONG MYUR BA'I NUS PA 'DRA BA YUL CAN GZHAN GANG LA'ANG MED PAS, NGES PAR BDE BA DE BSKYED DGOS SO,,
wylie: des na stong nyid kyi don gtan la 'babs tshul khyad med kyang de'i don sgom par byed pa na, ga-yas ga-yon gyi rlung dhU tIr btsud nas der thim pa'i dbang gis gtum mo 'bar bas byang sems bzhus pa'i bde ba chen pos stong pa'i don nges nas sgom pa'i lhan skyes kyis sgrib pa'i bag chags sbyong myur ba'i nus pa 'dra ba yul can gzhan gang la'ang med pas, nges par bde ba de bskyed dgos so
english: We can say thus that there is no difference between the open and secret teachings on the question of how we establish the fact that everything is empty.  When in the secret teachings we perform a meditation upon this fact, we utilize a feeling of great bliss--bliss which arises when we are able to get the right and left winds into the channel of dance, and dissolve there.  This brings the inner fire to blaze, which melts down the element of enlightenment, bringing on then the great bliss. We use this bliss to perceive the fact that things are empty of themselves.  This simultaneous bliss and voidness, as we meditate with it, has the capacity to rid us quickly of all the propensities we have within us for spiritual obstacles.  There is no other subject state of mind which can compare with this one--combined bliss and emptiness--and so the case is that we absolutely must reach this state of bliss.
